dtr.preservation: Original v6 seals/publications and the existing v7 DTRSEAL2 interpretation remain unchanged; the generic bounded predecessor descriptor authenticates subsequent epochs in Rust and JavaScript.

maximum_population.qualification: PocketIC virtual scheduling demonstrates timer cadence and bounded completion. Shared-host emulator wall rate is recorded separately and is not mainnet throughput.

browser_normal_lifeline_reconnect.failure: The shared PocketIC producer and certified gateway could not retain a playable lead. The browser repeatedly crossed the three-publication retention window and resynchronized, so Normal playback did not start within 60 seconds.
browser_normal_lifeline_reconnect.lifeline: NOT_RUN because the required Normal playback prerequisite failed.
browser_normal_lifeline_reconnect.qualification: This is a real bounded local failure, not represented as sustainable 1 tick/second performance. Chromium used user-scoped runtime libraries; no sudo, system installation or sandbox weakening was used.

performance.capacity_model: Compact run-length ownership, incremental counts, bounded/resumable topology, v5 bounded entity-pass batching, 1 MiB per public artifact, 8 MiB internal coordinator image, and disjoint overflow stable keys preserving legacy slots.

genuine_failures_corrected: The first maximum-population run exceeded the mistakenly shared 1 MiB internal image cap; internal images now use DTR's existing 8 MiB bound while public artifacts remain at 1 MiB.
The next run exposed per-ball durable serialization and reduced supported_milli to 695; bounded v5 entity-pass batching restored supported_milli to 1000 without changing public hashes.
The first Python tool-test invocation named a nonexistent module; the correct seven-test suite passed.
Strict integration Clippy found a manual inclusive-range comparison; the equivalent RangeInclusive check passed on rerun.
The browser initially lacked 13 shared libraries. Checksum-recorded Ubuntu Jammy packages were unpacked under ignored .work only; sandboxed Chromium then launched without system installation.
The first browser assertions exposed unformatted million-world dimensions and a sparse MOVE selection lost on each certified rerender; both UI defects were corrected before measuring playback.

The browser harness initially raced PocketIC live time and callback polling. The final run uses live wall time and bounded callback service, then records the production/delivery failure rather than weakening playback assertions.
external_blockers: DTR commit e1bfcf25071d11190d14f461288e12a21ca26cf8 and @dtr/timeline-runtime 0.14.0 are not remotely published. B2Z remains correctly pinned to published DTR 0.13.0 until the user publishes the immutable DTR revision/package.
acceptance_blockers: The representative four-ball sandboxed browser run cannot accumulate verified playback at the Normal target on the shared PocketIC host. Backend supported_milli fell to 726 and the browser repeatedly resynchronized across the three-publication retention window. Further production/persistence or delivery optimization is required before the million-cell release can be frozen.

deployment.mainnet_actions: None. No upgrade, transition, transfer, controller change, reset or reinstall was performed.
